q: I leave the Sun and reach your eyes in about eight minutes, and I weigh nothing at all. What am I?
explanation: Light covers the 150 million km in about 8.3 minutes. Photons have no mass. The solar wind takes days, and sound cannot cross empty space.

q: I have a tail but no body. I come back again and again, and the closer I get to the Sun, the longer I grow.
explanation: Sunlight boils ice off a comet, and the solar wind pushes that gas and dust into a tail pointing away from the Sun.

q: Every other planet borrowed the name of a god. I was named after the ground beneath your feet.
explanation: "Earth" comes from old words for soil and ground. The other planets carry Roman or Greek god names.

q: Half of me is always lit, but how much of that half you see changes all month long.
explanation: The Sun always lights one half of the Moon. Its phases are just how much of that lit half faces Earth.

q: I spin backwards compared with my neighbours, and one turn takes me longer than a whole trip round the Sun.
explanation: Venus rotates once every 243 Earth days, retrograde, but orbits the Sun in 225 days.

q: I am the biggest planet, and a storm wider than Earth has been raging on me since before your great-great-grandparents were born.
explanation: Jupiter's Great Red Spot has been watched continuously since at least the 1830s.

q: My gravity wins so completely that not even light can climb back out.
explanation: Inside the event horizon, escape speed is greater than the speed of light.

q: People call me a falling star, but I am only a pebble burning up as I rush through the air.
explanation: Most meteors are grains of dust or small rocks heated to glowing by friction with the atmosphere.

q: Sailors trusted me because I barely move all night, hanging over the north.
explanation: Polaris sits almost exactly above Earth's north rotation axis, so the sky seems to turn around it.

q: I am rusty red, and I hold the tallest volcano in the whole solar system.
explanation: Iron oxide dust colours Mars. Olympus Mons rises about 22 km, nearly three times Everest's height.

q: Twelve people have walked on me, and their footprints are still there because no wind blows them away.
explanation: The Apollo astronauts walked on the Moon from 1969 to 1972. With no air, nothing erodes their prints quickly.

q: I circle Earth about sixteen times a day, and on a clear evening you can watch me cross the sky in a few minutes.
explanation: The ISS orbits at about 400 km and laps the planet roughly every 92 minutes.

q: I was found in 1930, and I still have not finished a single lap of the Sun since.
explanation: Pluto takes about 248 years to orbit the Sun. Neptune, found in 1846, completed its first observed orbit in 2011.

q: I look like a solid hoop, but I am billions of icy pieces, each on its own orbit.
explanation: Saturn's rings are mostly water ice, from dust grains to house-sized chunks.

q: You live inside me, so you can only see me edge-on, as a faint band across the night.
explanation: Our galaxy is a flat disc. From inside it, the disc looks like a glowing strip of stars.

q: When a huge star dies I can outshine its whole galaxy for weeks.
explanation: A supernova releases as much light in weeks as the Sun will in its whole life.

q: I spin like a lighthouse, sweeping radio beams past Earth hundreds of times a second.
explanation: Pulsars are spinning neutron stars. Their beams sweep past us like a lighthouse.

q: I arrive when your half of Earth tilts toward the Sun, not when Earth is nearest to it.
explanation: Earth is actually closest to the Sun in early January. Tilt sets the seasons.

q: I happen when the Moon slides exactly between you and the Sun.
explanation: The Moon's shadow falls on Earth. It is about 400 times smaller than the Sun but also about 400 times closer.

q: I happen when Earth's shadow turns a full Moon copper red.
explanation: Sunlight bending through Earth's atmosphere reaches the Moon, filtered red, like every sunset at once.

q: I am ice that skips being liquid and turns straight into gas, so I make spooky stage fog.
explanation: Dry ice is frozen carbon dioxide. At normal air pressure it sublimes at about −78 °C.

q: I am the lightest element and the most common one in the universe.
explanation: About three quarters of the ordinary matter in the universe is hydrogen.

q: I put out most fires, yet poured on a burning pan of oil I make a fireball.
explanation: Water sinks under hot oil, boils instantly and throws burning oil into the air. Smother oil fires instead.

q: I am a metal, yet I am liquid on a cool day in your room.
explanation: Mercury melts at −39 °C. (Gallium melts in your hand at about 30 °C.)

q: I have no smell of my own, but companies add one to me so you notice when I leak.
explanation: LPG and natural gas are odourless. A sulfur compound is added to give the warning smell.

q: I pull the apple down and stop the Moon from drifting off.
explanation: Newton realised the same force works on a falling apple and the orbiting Moon.

q: Rub a balloon on your hair and I make it cling to the wall.
explanation: Rubbing moves electrons, leaving the balloon charged. The charge attracts the wall.

q: Air scatters me more than red, so I fill the daytime sky.
explanation: Shorter wavelengths scatter more. Violet scatters even more, but sunlight has less of it and our eyes are less sensitive to it.

q: On Earth I am found naturally as a solid, a liquid and a gas, all at once.
explanation: Glaciers, oceans and water vapour exist side by side across the planet.

q: Ice has less of me than liquid water, and that is why it floats.
explanation: Water expands by about 9% when it freezes, so ice is less dense and floats.

q: I travel faster through steel than through air, and not at all through empty space.
explanation: Sound is a vibration of matter. In steel it moves about 15 times faster than in air.

q: I am the hardest natural material, made of the same element as pencil lead.
explanation: Both diamond and graphite are pure carbon. Only the arrangement of the atoms differs.

q: I am the tiny engine in your cells that turns food into usable energy.
explanation: Mitochondria make ATP, the molecule cells spend as energy.

q: I am the green pigment that lets leaves catch sunlight.
explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light and reflects green.

q: I am the red protein that carries oxygen around your body.
explanation: Each haemoglobin molecule can carry four oxygen molecules.

q: I make up most of every breath you take, yet your body barely uses me.
explanation: Air is about 78% nitrogen. We breathe it in and out unchanged.

q: However big or small the circle, I stay exactly the same.
explanation: Any circle’s circumference divided by its diameter is π, about 3.14159.

q: Mix me with vinegar and I bubble up a science-fair volcano.
explanation: Sodium bicarbonate reacts with acetic acid to release carbon dioxide gas.

q: I sit at the centre of an atom and hold almost all of its mass.
explanation: Protons and neutrons are each about 1,800 times heavier than an electron.

q: Lightning heats the air so fast that it bursts outward, and you hear me.
explanation: A lightning channel reaches about 30,000 K in a split second. The shock wave is thunder.

q: I am frozen rain that bounced up and down inside a storm, gaining layers like an onion.
explanation: Updrafts carry hailstones back up through supercooled water many times. Cut one open to see the rings.

q: I am white and six-sided, and people say no two of me look alike.
explanation: Water molecules lock together in hexagons, so snow crystals grow with six-fold symmetry.

q: You see me with the Sun at your back and rain falling in front of you.
explanation: Each raindrop bends and reflects sunlight back toward you at about 42°.

q: I am a shimmering curtain in polar skies, painted when the solar wind hits the air.
explanation: Charged particles follow Earth's magnetic field toward the poles and make oxygen and nitrogen glow.

q: I look like water lying on a hot road ahead, but I vanish when you get close.
explanation: Hot air near the road bends light from the sky upward, so you see the sky reflected on the ground.

q: I appear on grass on clear, still nights, when the ground cools below the dew point.
explanation: The ground loses heat to the clear sky and water vapour condenses on it.

q: I am a spinning column of air that reaches down from a storm cloud to the ground.
explanation: Tornadoes grow from rotating thunderstorms and are usually only tens to hundreds of metres wide.

q: Over the Indian Ocean I am a cyclone, over the Atlantic a hurricane, and near Japan a typhoon.
explanation: All three names describe the same kind of storm: a warm-ocean low with spiralling winds.

q: I am a giant wave made by an earthquake or landslide, not by the wind.
explanation: A tsunami moves the whole depth of the ocean and can cross a sea at jet-plane speed.

q: I am the seasonal wind shift that brings most of India its rain.
explanation: In summer the land heats faster than the sea, drawing moist ocean air inland.

q: I tell forecasters the pressure of the air.
explanation: Falling pressure often means bad weather is coming.

q: I spin my little cups to tell you how fast the wind blows.
explanation: The faster the wind, the faster the cups turn.

q: I was once lava or magma, and I hardened as I cooled.
explanation: Granite cooled slowly underground; basalt cooled quickly at the surface.

q: I am sand and mud pressed into layers over ages, and I often hide fossils.
explanation: Sandstone, shale and limestone form this way, trapping remains of living things.

q: Heat and pressure changed me without melting me, the way limestone becomes marble.
explanation: Metamorphic rocks recrystallise deep underground.

q: I am melted rock, but I only keep my name while I stay underground.
explanation: Once it erupts onto the surface, magma is called lava.

q: I am the layer you stand on, thinner compared with Earth than an apple's skin is to the apple.
explanation: The crust is 5 to 70 km thick. Earth’s radius is about 6,371 km.

q: My slow drifting builds the Himalayas and shakes the ground in earthquakes.
explanation: The Indian plate is still pushing north into Asia, a few centimetres each year.

q: I am the highest mountain above sea level.
explanation: Everest stands about 8,849 m above sea level.

q: Measured from my base on the sea floor, I am taller than Everest.
explanation: Mauna Kea in Hawaii rises over 10,000 m from its base, though only about 4,200 m is above sea level.

q: I am the largest ocean, covering about a third of the whole planet.
explanation: The Pacific is larger than all the land on Earth put together.

q: I am the largest hot desert on Earth.
explanation: The Sahara covers about 9 million km². The largest desert of all is cold: Antarctica.

q: I am a whole continent, and I count as a desert because so little snow falls on me.
explanation: Deserts are defined by low precipitation, not heat. The South Pole gets very little snow each year.

q: I am the river that gave the subcontinent its name.
explanation: "India" comes from Sindhu, the old name of the Indus, through Persian and Greek.

q: I am the line at 0° latitude.
explanation: The equator splits Earth into northern and southern hemispheres.

q: I am the line at 0° longitude, running through Greenwich.
explanation: It was agreed at a conference in 1884 as the zero point for longitude.

q: I cross India, and in June the noon Sun stands straight overhead along me.
explanation: At the June solstice the Sun is overhead at about 23.4° N, matching Earth's tilt.

q: I am the smallest number that 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 all divide exactly.
A rocket and its fuel cost 1,100 credits together. The rocket costs 1,000 credits more than the fuel. What does the fuel cost?
explanation: Fuel = x, rocket = x + 1,000. So 2x + 1,000 = 1,100 and x = 50.

q: Three drones plant three trees in three minutes. How long do thirty drones take to plant thirty trees?
explanation: Each drone plants one tree in three minutes, however many drones work at once.

q: Moss on a station window doubles every day and covers the whole window on day 20. On which day was it half covered?
explanation: It doubles from half to full in one day.

q: Multiply me by any number you like and the answer is still me.
explanation: Zero times anything is zero.

q: What comes next: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, …
explanation: Each number is the sum of the two before it (the Fibonacci sequence): 5 + 8 = 13.

q: A cube has how many edges?
explanation: 4 on top, 4 on the bottom, and 4 upright ones.

q: On the Moon, which weighs more: 1 kg of moon dust or 1 kg of steel?
explanation: Equal masses in the same gravity weigh the same. On the Moon each weighs about a sixth of its Earth weight.

q: It is 9 o'clock now. What will the clock show in 100 hours?
explanation: 100 hours is 4 days and 4 hours. Four hours after 9 is 1.

q: I am a three-digit number whose digits add up to 1.
explanation: The only way three digits sum to 1 with a non-zero first digit is 1, 0, 0.

q: In 12 hours, how many times do the hour and minute hands of a clock overlap?
explanation: The minute hand laps the hour hand every 12/11 hours, so 11 times, not 12.

q: Add up every whole number from 1 to 100.
explanation: Pair 1 with 100, 2 with 99, and so on: 50 pairs of 101 = 5,050.

q: How many squares of every size are there on a chessboard?
In a rover race, you overtake the rover in second place. What place are you in now?
explanation: You took second place. The leader is still ahead of you.

q: With only a 3-litre tank and a 5-litre tank, can you measure exactly 4 litres?
explanation: Fill 5, pour into 3 (2 left). Empty 3, pour the 2 in. Fill 5 again and top up the 3: 4 litres remain.

q: How many months of the year contain a 28th day?
explanation: Every month has at least 28 days. February simply stops soon after.

q: A floating dock has a ladder with rungs 30 cm apart. The tide rises 90 cm. How many more rungs are underwater?
explanation: The dock floats, so it rises with the water.

q: Which of these is prime?
explanation: 91 = 7 × 13, 93 = 3 × 31 and 99 = 9 × 11. 97 has no factors but 1 and itself.

q: What is half of two plus two?
explanation: Half of two is 1, then add 2. Division comes before addition.

q: Divide 30 by a half, then add 10.
explanation: Dividing by ½ doubles: 30 ÷ ½ = 60, plus 10 = 70.

q: How many small cubes build one 3 × 3 × 3 cube?
explanation: 3 × 3 × 3 = 27. (26 can be seen from outside; one hides in the middle.)

q: You have a 4-minute and a 7-minute sand timer. Can you time exactly 9 minutes?
explanation: Start both. Flip the 4 when it ends (4 min). When the 7 ends (7 min), flip it. When the 4 ends again (8 min), flip the 7: it runs 1 more minute, to 9.

q: Which is the odd one out: 2, 3, 5, 9, 11?
explanation: All the others are prime. 9 = 3 × 3.

q: Which is the odd one out: Mercury, Venus, Jupiter, Mars?
explanation: Jupiter is a gas giant. The others are rocky planets.

q: Which is the odd one out: iron, copper, oxygen, gold?
explanation: Oxygen is a non-metal gas. The rest are metals.

q: Which is the odd one out: whale, shark, dolphin, seal?
explanation: Sharks are fish. The others are mammals that breathe air.

q: Which is the odd one out: triangle, square, circle, pentagon?
explanation: A circle has no straight sides or corners.

q: An astronaut on the Moon drops a hammer and a feather at the same moment. Which lands first?
explanation: With no air resistance, everything falls at the same rate. Apollo 15 showed this on camera in 1971.

q: Why do tears not run down your cheeks in orbit?
answer: They cling to your eyes in a ball
explanation: In free fall nothing pulls tears down, so surface tension holds them in a growing blob.

q: A pilot flies 1 km south, 1 km east, then 1 km north, and lands where she started. Where did she start?
explanation: At the North Pole every direction is south, and going north again brings you back to the point.

q: A photo is sent from Mars while Mars is 225 million km away. About how long until it reaches Earth?
explanation: Radio travels at light speed: 225,000,000 ÷ 300,000 ≈ 750 s, about 12.5 minutes.

q: Why do astronauts on the ISS see about sixteen sunrises every day?
answer: They orbit Earth every 90 minutes or so
choices: The Sun moves faster in space
explanation: Every lap passes from night side to day side once.

q: Why do you weigh a tiny bit less at the equator than at the poles?
choices: You are closer to the Sun
explanation: Spin flings you outward slightly, and the equatorial bulge puts you farther from the centre.

q: A metal spoon and a wooden spoon sit in the same room. Why does the metal one feel colder?
answer: Metal carries heat away from your hand faster
explanation: Both are at room temperature. Your skin senses heat flow, not temperature.

q: Why does the Moon look bigger near the horizon?
explanation: Measure it with a coin at arm’s length: the size is the same. Your brain judges it against the landscape.

q: If you could fold a 0.1 mm sheet of paper in half 42 times, how thick would it be?
answer: Thicker than the distance to the Moon
explanation: 0.1 mm × 2⁴² ≈ 440,000 km. Doubling grows fast.

q: Two rovers 10 km apart drive toward each other at 5 km/h each. A drone flies back and forth between them at 20 km/h until they meet. How far does it fly?
explanation: They meet after one hour, and the drone flies at 20 km/h for that hour.

q: A station clock gains 5 seconds a day. After how many days is it a full minute fast?
Two spheres look and weigh the same, but one is hollow. How can you tell which, without breaking them?
explanation: The hollow one has its mass farther out, so it resists spinning and rolls down more slowly.

q: Why does a steel ship float when a steel ball sinks?
answer: Its shape pushes aside a lot of water
explanation: A floating object pushes aside its own weight of water. A hollow hull can push aside much more than a solid ball.

q: An ice cube floats in a glass filled to the brim. When it melts, what happens?
explanation: Floating ice already pushes aside exactly its own weight of water.

q: Which roof keeps a house cooler in summer sun?
explanation: White reflects most sunlight; black absorbs it as heat.

q: You see lightning and count 6 seconds before the thunder. About how far away was it?
explanation: Sound covers about 343 m each second: 6 × 343 ≈ 2 km.

q: Why do your ears pop when a plane climbs?
explanation: Air trapped behind your eardrum has to even out with the cabin air as its pressure falls.

q: If there are so many stars, why is the night sky dark?
answer: The universe has a finite age
explanation: Light from very distant stars hasn't had time to reach us, and expansion stretches it out of view. This is Olbers' paradox.

q: What shape is a candle flame aboard the space station?
explanation: On Earth hot air rises and stretches the flame. In free fall it spreads evenly in all directions.

q: I am the crushed-rock dust that holds the astronauts' bootprints on the Moon.
explanation: Billions of years of tiny impacts ground the Moon’s surface into a fine powder.

q: I was a rock from space, and unlike a meteor, I made it all the way to the ground.
explanation: Meteors burn up in the air. The pieces that survive and land are meteorites.

q: I am the band between Mars and Jupiter where leftover rocks circle the Sun.
explanation: Its total mass is only a few percent of our Moon’s.

q: I am a dwarf planet, and I live in the asteroid belt.
explanation: Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt, about 940 km across.

q: I am a moon with volcanoes erupting right now, squeezed and warmed by Jupiter's pull.
explanation: Tides from Jupiter flex Io's interior, keeping it the most volcanic body known.

q: I am the only moon with a thick atmosphere, and I have lakes of liquid methane.
explanation: Saturn's moon Titan has rain, rivers and seas, but made of methane and ethane.

q: I am an icy moon of Jupiter hiding a salty ocean under my crust.
explanation: Europa’s ocean may hold twice the water of all Earth’s oceans.

q: I am the planet that rolls around the Sun on my side.
explanation: Uranus is tilted about 98°, perhaps from an ancient collision.

q: I am the windiest planet, with gusts faster than 2,000 km/h.
explanation: Neptune's winds are the fastest measured in the solar system.

q: I am the hottest planet, even though I am not the closest to the Sun.
explanation: A thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat, keeping the surface near 465 °C.

q: I am the closest planet to the Sun, yet my nights drop far below freezing.
explanation: With almost no air to hold heat, Mercury swings from about 430 °C to −180 °C.

q: I am a small star, cooler and redder than the Sun, and the most common kind in our galaxy.
explanation: About three in four stars near the Sun are red dwarfs, too faint to see without a telescope.

q: In about five billion years the Sun will swell into me.
explanation: The Sun is too light to explode. It will swell, shed its outer layers and leave a white dwarf.

q: I sound like a measure of time, but a light-year is a unit of what?
explanation: A light-year is how far light travels in a year: about 9.46 trillion km.

q: I hold an atomic nucleus together even though its protons push each other away.
explanation: Over tiny distances it is about 100 times stronger than the electric push.

q: I power the Sun by joining light atoms into heavier ones.
explanation: In the core, hydrogen nuclei fuse into helium, turning a little mass into a lot of energy.

q: Nuclear power stations use me, splitting heavy atoms apart.
explanation: Uranium nuclei split, releasing heat and more neutrons that split more nuclei.

q: I make party balloons float, and I am element number two.
explanation: Helium is lighter than air and does not burn, unlike hydrogen.

q: My chemical symbol is Fe.
explanation: Fe comes from the Latin "ferrum".

q: My chemical symbol is Au, from the Latin word for shining dawn.
explanation: "Aurum" gives gold its symbol Au.

q: My chemical symbol is Na.
explanation: Na comes from the Latin "natrium".

q: I am the pH of pure water at 25 °C.
explanation: pH 7 is neutral. Lower is acidic, higher is basic.

q: I am the unit of force, named after the man who described gravity.
explanation: One newton accelerates 1 kg by 1 m/s every second.

q: I am the unit of electrical resistance.
explanation: Named after Georg Ohm. Voltage = current × resistance.

q: I am the dark opening in your eye that widens in the dark and shrinks in bright light.
explanation: The iris muscles change the pupil’s size to control how much light gets in.

q: I am the largest organ of the human body.
explanation: Skin covers about 2 m² in an adult.

q: I am the bony helmet that protects your brain.
explanation: The skull is made of plates that fuse during childhood.

q: How many chambers does a human heart have?
explanation: Two atria receive blood and two ventricles pump it out.

q: I start my life breathing water and end it breathing air.
explanation: Tadpoles breathe with gills, then grow lungs as they become frogs.

q: I am the change that turns a caterpillar into a butterfly.
explanation: Inside the chrysalis, much of the caterpillar breaks down and rebuilds as a butterfly.

q: I turn sunlight, water and carbon dioxide into sugar, and breathe out oxygen.
explanation: Almost all the oxygen in our air was made this way.

q: I am seen by day as a pale ghost, though I give off no light of my own.
explanation: The Moon only reflects sunlight, and it is often in the sky during the day.

q: I am a cloud that touches the ground.
explanation: Fog is made of the same tiny water droplets as a cloud, just at ground level.

q: I am the brightest point of light in the night sky after the Moon, and I am not a star.
explanation: Venus is bright because it is close and covered in reflective clouds.

q: I am the brightest true star in the night sky.
explanation: Sirius is about 8.6 light-years away and about 25 times as bright as the Sun.

q: I go up when the rain comes down.
explanation: A plain everyday riddle: you open an umbrella when it rains.

q: The more of me you take, the more you leave behind on the beach.
explanation: Each step you take leaves a footprint behind.

q: I have lanes but no swimmers, and I take you everywhere without moving an inch.
explanation: A road has lanes and leads to places, but stays put.

q: I get wetter the more I dry.
explanation: A towel absorbs water as it dries you.

q: I can be cracked, made, told and played.
explanation: You crack, make, tell and play a joke. An egg can be cracked but not told.

q: I am taken before you get me, and I always show you as you were a moment ago.
explanation: You take a photo, then you get it. It shows the past, even if only by a second.

q: I have a spine but no bones, and pages but no website.
explanation: A book has a spine and pages.

q: I have one eye but never see, and a thread runs through me.
explanation: The hole in a needle is called its eye.

q: I run around a field all day but never move.
explanation: A fence "runs" around the edge of a field.

q: I am full of stars, but I am not the sky. Turn my pages and you travel the heavens.
explanation: A star atlas, or star chart, maps the sky on paper.

q: Feed me and I live, give me water and I die.
explanation: Fire needs fuel. Water cools it below burning and cuts off air.

q: I can travel round the world while staying in a corner.
explanation: A stamp sits in the corner of an envelope and goes wherever the letter goes.

q: True or false: a fully pumped tyre weighs a little more than the same tyre when flat.
explanation: Pumped air has mass. A fully inflated tyre is a little heavier than a flat one.

q: To catch a spacecraft ahead of you on the same orbit, you first slow down. Why does that work?
explanation: Slowing drops you to a smaller orbit, where you lap faster, then you speed up to rise and meet it.

q: I am a shadow that falls on the Moon each month at full Moon, but only sometimes. Why only sometimes?
explanation: The Moon’s orbit tilts about 5°, so usually it passes above or below Earth’s shadow.

q: Why does a cup of water left out slowly disappear even without boiling?
explanation: The fastest molecules at the surface escape as vapour at any temperature.

q: Why do you see lightning before you hear thunder?
choices: Your eyes are faster than ears
explanation: Light reaches you almost instantly; sound needs about 3 seconds per kilometre.

q: A balloon is filled indoors, then taken outside on a freezing day. What happens to it?
explanation: Cold gas takes up less space at the same pressure.

q: If Earth stopped spinning but kept orbiting, how long would a day last?
explanation: One side would face the Sun for half a year, then the other side for the next half.
